We propose S.C.O.R.E. (Safety, Consensus & Context, Objectivity, Reproducibility, Explainability), a five-dimensional framework for structured expert evaluation of LLM-generated healthcare responses. S.C.O.R.E. has been validated against quantitative metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, and BERTScore) using three LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 4 Sonnet, and DeepSeek) across ophthalmology, medication, and anesthesia. While quantitative metrics frequently misclassified clinically appropriate responses as inaccurate, S.C.O.R.E. demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α 0.745) in the hyperparameter-optimized domain and detected large effect sizes (Cliff's δ 0.68-0.92) reflecting optimization status. Model rankings reversed across specialties-GPT-4o excelled in ophthalmology (optimized domain), while others in non-optimized domains-thus domain-specific tuning is both necessary and detectable through expert evaluation. S.C.O.R.E.'s correlation between framework reliability and optimization status validates its utility for iterative model refinement. {"requested_url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/master/docs/architecture.md", "source_revision": "69e8955060f292d0d1e900314d626de9063e219c", "running_revision": "9c2b2de3f89bd61d60e55f47172b96eb10be3c1e", "source_search": "", "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/69e8955060f292d0d1e900314d626de9063e219c/docs/architecture.md", "scope": "raw source-controlled WAKE repository text", "excerpt": "# Architecture and limits

See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. 3: WAKE✳︎ is infrastructure for durable, accountable work across interchangeable
4: models, runtimes, and people. Research is its first application. Its name asks
5: us to consider what remains after an interaction ends:
6: 
7: > A wave describes possibilities. A wake carries the consequences of what has occurred.
8: 
9: This is the starting image for the **Quantum Wake Function** metaphor. The
10: architecture gives that image a practical expression: work can leave an
11: inspectable history that survives the intelligence that produced it.
12: 
13: ## Waves and wakes
14: 
15: Imagine a boat crossing a quiet lake. Its wake is the disturbance left by its
16: passage. The boat may be gone while that disturbance continues to spread,
17: interact with other disturbances, and affect another boat's passage.
18: 
19: A wake is both evidence of the past and an influence on the future.
20: 
21: The distinction concerns what we are looking at: a wave's form and propagation,
22: or a disturbance in relation to the passage that produced it. A wake contains
23: waves; ordinary water waves also have causes and consequences. The opening
24: sentence is a metaphor, not a physical classification of waves as possibilities
25: and wakes as facts. Nor does a water wake preserve a complete, permanent account
26: of its cause.
